bar_001: You can recognise it by its low, heavy grey trunk, leaning where it reaches past the holm oaks for light. It stands in the gardens of Piazza Umberto I, five minutes from the central station.
bar_002: You can recognise it by its swollen grey base, like an elephant's foot, standing a few metres from the ombu in the same flowerbed. It stands in the gardens of Piazza Umberto I.
bar_003: You can recognise it by its thick trunk, close to six metres round, inside a fenced bed behind a low concrete wall people climb over. It stands at the corner of Corso Alcide De Gasperi and Via Ugo La Malfa, in Carrassi.
bar_004: You can recognise it by the way it stands right in front of the old masseria gate, so awkwardly placed that carts once had to work around it. It stands on Viale della Pineta, in the centre of Quasano.
bar_005: You can recognise it as the oak standing in the olive and almond groves inside the masseria's walls. It stands at Masseria Storica Pilapalucci, in Contrada Pilapalucci, Toritto.
